item.title: Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
item.description: By Adeola Badru The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a campaign balloon at the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred controversy, raising questions about the governor’s political alignment ahead of the 2027 general elections. The balloon, hoisted at the rally ground around the historic Mapo Hall, featured images of prominent political figures, including Makinde, who is not a member of the APC and has yet to publicly declare support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. Its appearance attracted attention at the campaign venue, particularly as Makinde is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). The governor’s inclusion on the balloon raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the display and the political message it was intended to convey. However, it was not immediately clear who authorised the inclusion of Makinde’s image or the circumstances that led to its appearance at the APC rally. Meanwhile, President Tinubu has urged residents of Oyo State to sustain their support for the APC, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Speaking at the rally, Tinubu promised increased investments in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply, while endorsing Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in the state. The President also announced plans to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, disclosing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer, Yutong, to reopen the facility for public transport vehicle production and establish an automobile assembly plant. “For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” Tinubu said. He also assured residents of improved electricity supply, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team. “You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team,” he said. Tinubu urged the electorate to remain committed to the APC, recalling their support for the party in the previous election. “You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” he said. He stressed the need to prioritise education and agriculture to create opportunities for younger generations. “We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said. The President also criticised opposition parties, describing them as “mediocre”, and urged voters not to be distracted by them

item.title: From global blacklist to international recognition: Tinubu’s unprecedented aviation transformation
item.description: By Seyi Bakare 91.45% ICAO safety rating breaks all previous records; five international airports achieve full certification; $850m trapped airline funds cleared; Emirates returns; indigenous airlines empowered as massive infrastructure renewal takes off. Nigeria’s aviation industry is undergoing one of the most remarkable transformations in its history, with the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu recording unprecedented milestones in aviation safety, airport infrastructure, international relations, airline operations and the restoration of investor confidence. What was once an industry struggling with international credibility, restricted access to aircraft financing, trapped foreign airline revenues, deteriorating infrastructure and regulatory deficiencies is gradually emerging as a more competitive and internationally respected aviation destination. The transformation is not merely reflected in government announcements or policy pronouncements. It is increasingly evident in measurable improvements in safety oversight, the return of major international airlines, renewed access to aircraft leasing markets, the expansion of indigenous carriers and substantial investments in airport infrastructure across the country. Perhaps the most compelling evidence of this turnaround is Nigeria’s historic 91.45 per cent Effective Implementation score in the International Civil Aviation Organisation’s (ICAO) safety oversight assessment conducted in April 2026. The achievement represents Nigeria’s highest aviation safety rating in history, placing the country significantly above the global average of 70.4 per cent and the West African regional average of 61.1 per cent. It is a remarkable departure from the approximately 70 per cent performance that had characterised previous assessments. For an industry where safety standards determine international confidence, investment decisions and operational credibility, the improvement represents a significant national achievement. The administration has also achieved full aerodrome certification of Nigeria’s five international airports in Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Port Harcourt and Enugu for the first time in the country’s history. These accomplishments demonstrate the impact of deliberate regulatory reforms, institutional strengthening and investments in modern aviation infrastructure. Rebuilding Nigeria’s aviation gateways Beyond regulatory improvements, the Tinubu administration has embarked on an ambitious programme to modernise the country’s airport infrastructure. The flagship project is the comprehensive reconstruction and modernisation of Terminal 1 at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, with a Federal Government commitment of N712.3 billion. The project, which is more than 50 per cent complete as of November 2026, is designed to transform Nigeria’s busiest international gateway into a modern aviation facility capable of meeting contemporary international standards The scope includes redesign

item.title: James Talarico fires cannon, chats with cheerleaders on Texas football sideline
item.description: Senator James Talarico greets Texas cheerleaders as he attends the Texas v. Arkansas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Texas' new soon-to-be senator enjoyed a victory lap on the Texas football sideline Saturday. James Talarico , who defeated Ken Paxton in November to become Texas' first Democrat senator since 1993, spent time near the field at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium before the Longhorns hosted Arkansas. Talarico was joined by his girlfriend, Brianna Menard. The two chatted with Texas cheerleaders pregame, and Talarico took part in a classic Longhorns tradition as he stood behind and fired Smokey the Cannon. GOLDEN: How the hell did the Texas Longhorns win that? The hard way. FILM REVIEW: How Arch Manning's legs saved Longhorns at LSU Saturday marked Talarico's first time at DKR this season, though he's watched each contest this season, per his office. Talarico also attended a Texas home game in 2025, and he shared a brief comment on his appearance Saturday through a spokesperson. "Hook 'em horns." Senator James Talarico fires Smokey the Cannon as he attends the Texas v. Arkansas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Talarico wasn't the only Texas politician spotted on the sideline. Outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott appeared near the field at DKR pregame in what was his second public appearance since losing his race to governor-elect Gina Hinojosa. Abbott appeared at a graduation ceremony Friday for 62 Texas Department of Public Safety officers in Cedar Park, and he previously attended Texas' loss to Oklahoma last month, when he handed out the Red River Rivalry trophy to the Sooners after their 27-24 victory at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas. item.title: Peyton Miller dazzles in playoff debut with New England Revolution
item.description: Peyton Miller dazzles in playoff debut with New England Revolution By José Nuñez Welcome to the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, Peyton Miller . The New England Revolution 's rising homegrown star stole the show during Saturday's Round One opener, causing an own goal and scoring a superb volley to secure a 2-0 Game 1 win over the Philadelphia Union at Gillette Stadium. “I think that just shows how much he has grown in maturity, if I can say it like that. It really shows that he is ready to compete,” head coach Marko Mitrović said of Miller's standout effort. “Yes, he is a really young player, but he is converting from potential to being a performer. That is what a performer does.” Big first impression Miller memorable playoff debut marked another milestone in a season full of them for the 19-year-old. Amid producing a career-best 7g/9a, the versatile wingback broke into the US men's national team in September and placed sixth in the 2026 22 Under 22 rankings. And in New England's first playoff appearance in three years, Miller led the Revs to their first postseason victory since 2020. “It’s surreal playing for my boyhood club, so I’m just thankful for everything and all glory to God. I thank the fans for all the support today," said Miller, who became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in playoff history. "My parents, my friends, are all here, so this is special.” On to Philadelphia Miller and the Revolution can close out Round One when the Best-of-3 Series moves to Philadelphia's Subaru Park for Game 2 on Nov. 28 (4:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). However, they're not taking anything for granted. That especially applies against an opponent that was dominant throughout the second half of the season behind the inspired play of teenage phenom Cavan Sullivan , Golden Boot presented by Audi contender Milan Iloski and others. “Philadelphia is a very demanding team, a team that keeps you on your toes for all 90 minutes," warned Mitrović. "Those games with Philly are always games of margins, and we just have to ensure that those margins go on our side.” WATCH: Peyton Miller & Revs take Game 1 vs. Philadelphia

item.title: Bengals' DB fined for taunting penalty vs Steelers
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle was fined $11,941 for unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting during the second quarter of their NFL Week 10 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . NBC Sports analyst and former Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth was critical of Battle for the penalty. Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss in 2025. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Bengals' DB fined for taunting penalty vs Steelers

item.title: Praises provoke miracles, by Funmi Komolafe
item.description: Beloved, let’s thank God that we are gradually moving to the end of 2026. May the LORD see us to the end of the year joyfully in Jesus name. We might have heard of the eleventh hour miracle which some have interpreted to mean the miracle that happens when hope is lost. It is miracle when the benefactor does not expect it. When a woman gets pregnant at age 63 or any age after 45, it is a last minute miracle. It could also be miracle that one does not deserve but got one because of the mercy of God. An example is the labourer that was hired when work was almost completed but got the same pay as those that had worked their hearts out. Matthew 16 vs. 8-11: (KJV)“ So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first. And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny. But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny. And when they had received it, they murmured against the good man of the house”. Brethren, when you receive an eleventh hour miracle, some people would grumble. They would express doubts, some might even be unhappy but they would be unable to stop the work of God. The labourer in the above quoted passage, got an eleventh hour miracle by the mercy of the master of the vineyard. You too can receive an eleventh hour miracle by the mercy of God. You can also provoke yours with Praises. How do I know? Psalm 22 vs. 3-4 gives me the answer. It states, “ But thou are holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel. Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them”. When we praise God with faith, we should know that God would not watch you praise him and do nothing. The LORD would definitely take an action on your behalf when you praise Him. King David, the shepherd boy that God made a king also knew that God is moved to action when he is praised hence David wrote many Psalms of praise to God. Psalm 34 vs. 1-3 is my witness. “ I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth. My soul shall make her boast in the LORD; the humble shall hear therof, and be glad. O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together”. If you still have doubts, remember King Jehoshaphat used praises to provoke God to deal with enemies when three kings that were too strong for him rose against him. Like any human being, Jehoshaphat feared. He cried to God in prayer but his last instrument was Praise. 2 Chronicles 20 vs. 21 &22 tells us what happened. “ And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the LORD; for his mercy endureth for ever. item.title: Bearcats bowl-eligble for a 2nd straight season, where do they go?
item.description: The Cincinnati Bearcats 35-28 win over Colorado gives them six wins and makes them bowl-eligible for the second straight season. Cole Tabb ran for 120 yards and two touchdowns and had seven receptions for 110 yards and two more scores. JC French IV, one of the 22 seniors playing their last game at Nippert, was 18-for-19 for 208 yards with two touchdown passes to Tabb plus 38 rushing yards and a score. “It means a ton, it's crazy," French said. "It's the last home game ever, a surreal moment. I am happy for the rest of these seniors.” UC has now qualified for a bowl bid in 14 of its last 19 seasons, including four New Year's Six bowls and the 2021 College Football Playoff semifinal appearance against Alabama in the Goodyear Cotton Bowl. Coming into the Nov. 21 game vs. Colorado , these were the bowl projections for the Bearcats: ESPN's Mark Schlabach – The Radiance Technologies Independence Bowl in Shreveport. The bowl is set for Dec. 22 on ESPN at 7:30 (Central)/8:30 (Eastern). Schlabach has UC playing Oregon State on ESPN. ESPN's Kyle Bonagura – Bonagura also sees UC in the Independence Bowl in Shreveport Dec. 22, but with a different matchup. He sees the Bearcats against the Washington Huskies on ESPN at 7:30 (Central)/8:30 (Eastern). USA Today – The Cactus Bowl in Tempe. This would be an interesting matchup for Bearcats fans as they have UC vs. Wisconsin. Potentially, it's Scott Satterfield vs. Luke Fickell at Mountain America Stadium with a 7:30 (Eastern) kickoff on ABC. New York Times/Athletic – Another Independence Bowl prediction Dec. 22 in Shreveport with an 8:30 (Eastern) kickoff on ESPN. They see the Bearcats against Stanford. UC is 10-13 all-time in bowl games but has dropped the last four (Peach Bowl, Cotton Bowl, Fenway Bowl, Liberty Bowl). The Bearcats last prevailed in a bowl game on Jan. 2, 2020, beating Boston College 38-6 in the Birmingham Bowl at Legion Field. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Bearcats bowl-eligble for a 2nd straight season, where do they go?

item.title: NBA officials miss Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds late in Bucks' loss
item.description: PHILADELPHIA - The Milwaukee Bucks haven't had a lot go right for them during the course of this season, especially in the midst of a current 13-game losing streak following a 132-129 loss to Philadelphia at the Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov. 21. But they were on the receiving end of a brutal missed call that could have determined the outcome of the game in the final seconds. Trailing 130-129 with 4.8 seconds left, the 76ers were inbounding opposite of their bench following a timeout. All of the game referees were watching LeBron James inbound, and then positioned around the 76ers basket. Only James floated the inbound pass deep toward the opposite end to Joel Embiid, and as the big man collected the ball and tried to evade an intentional foul from Tyler Herro, he stepped out of bounds. Only no one was there to see it but the Bucks' bench, and the fans in that corner. No whistle was blown, and Herro eventually fouled Embiid with 1.5 seconds left. Though the Bucks did not have a challenge, that is not something that could be reviewed had Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins had one. "Well, Embiid, he did step out of bounds," Herro said. "But for ref, it is a tough play. 'Cause the ball was being taken out on the other side of the court. For him to see that you've got to have a ref on that baseline. So it was a tough call, a tough play to see as a ref. So, I get that one." Brayden Burries wasn't in that corner, but saw the video of the play later. "He was out of bounds, but you know, they're humans, they miss calls," Burries said. "It just so happened it was a crucial call. But, it's OK." While the officials did miss the call, it's what happened in the immediate moments afterward that inevitably hurt the Bucks even more. Herro was trailing Embiid trying to intentionally foul, but when he saw Embiid step out, he instinctively pulled up. As soon as he realized there was no whistle, he committed the foul with 1.5 seconds left. "It looked like Tyler thought, or the team, that he stepped out of bounds," Jaime Jaquez Jr. "I didn't even see what happened but obviously I believe him. I think he kind of like slowed down because he thought they were going to call it, but I don't think there were any refs on that side. Which is, weird. But, I don't know where they're supposed to be but that was an important view for them to take a look at. I don't know." Shortly thereafter, Herro's buzzer beating attempt to tie the game was ruled no good as the ball left his hand a split second too late. "I just had to get the shot off a little bit quicker," Herro said. "I thought I had a little bit more time. Coach drew up a great play for me. I had the shot I wanted, I made it, just gotta be able to get it off on time next time." This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: NBA officials miss Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds late in Bucks' loss

item.title: Being one step ahead of an opportunist
item.description: By Bunmi Sofola SYLVIA admitted that her parents’ marriage and the stoic way her mum yielded her position as the first wife to a much younger and ambitious woman prepared her for the way she handled her relationship with men. Her story: “When a man suddenly discovers he’s scaled the ladder of success faster than he’d envisaged, what does he do when he gets to the top? Chuck his frumpy wife for a more sophisticated model that’s what! And it happened to my mother – a stark illiterate my father too couldn’t read or write, but he was a fairly successful cocoa farmer and although we weren’t exactly rolling in the lap of luxury, we were the envy of our small town – talk about big fish in a small pond indeed! “My dad had been on the war-path with the leadership of the Pentecostal Church we attended. Things finally got to a head, and he broke away to found his own church. A chunk of the congregation from the former church went with him and in a couple of years, his church had ballooned into something he himself never envisaged. As donations kept on pouring in from far and wide, he built a mini estate, installed my mother and her children (four of us) in one of the chalets, then got married to a school certificate holder and made her his main wife. His excuse was that he needed an educated ally to go through the books of the church and welcome visitors in a presentable way. “I don’t want to go through the rage and resentment we from my mother’s side felt as we witnessed this imposter parade herself as an intellectual. My poor father didn’t know that he was the laughing stock of the congregation who sniggered at the clumsy speeches his ‘educated’ wife always made, riddled with mistakes. “I was lucky to have a sharp brain and qualified as a lawyer. But I wasn’t lucky in my choice of a husband. Eventually my marriage hit the rocks after five years and two children. The man I had my third child for wasn’t much better, but I was lucky to meet this influential projects director of a parastatal and my life changed for the better. He took care of all my financial needs and was almost twenty years older than I was. “It is amazing what some women put up with for money. This man was fat and flabby. Whenever he slept over and I watched him asleep with his mouth so wide open I could see his missing teeth and the fillings in some of the rest snoring away without a care in the world. I felt really repulsed. He was definitely not a sight to light the fire in any virile woman’s loins, but he was kind and generous. Let’s face it, he was in his late fifties after all and it must be quite exhausting making love to his wife and God knows who else all the time! “When he was retired and went into politics, I was often with him and through his contacts, I was able to land into the midst of the heavies. item.title: Illinois falls to No.13 Iowa on Senior Night
item.description: Champaign, Ill. – The scoreboard might not reflect it, but this was a very tight game for roughly 3 ½ quarters. It didn’t end up going Illinois’ way, but the Illini gave No. 13 Iowa a run for their money. Illinois (6-5) fell to the visiting Hawkeyes 34-17, being shut out in the second half. After both teams traded field goals to open the game, it was the Hawkeyes (9-2) that found the end zone first. The score came via LJ Phillips, who set up his 2-yard rushing touchdown with his massive run just two plays before. Phillips, who finished the game with 150 rushing yards, shrugged off multiple Illini defenders on the 30-yard run. The Illini, however, answered with their own big play just minutes later. It was Brayden Trimble who found the end zone first for the Illini. Houser found Trimble on a short crossing route that would normally just pick up ten or so yards. But that wasn’t what Trimble did. He somehow tiptoed his way to a 75-yard touchdown. The scene was truly incredible at Gies Memorial Stadium. Every time you thought he was about to get tackled or step out of bounds, he just kept going. The ensuing review upheld that he did indeed stay in the field of play, much to the delight of the home crowd. The next two touchdowns would both come with some dramatic reviews right on the goal line. First, for Iowa, Addison Ostrenga took a pass to the right side of the Illinois end zone and extended to try to cross the plane. However, he lost control of the ball, and the play was ruled a touchback for the Illini, as the ball went out of the end zone. The play was then overturned after further review, and the Hawkeyes scored moments later. But the Illini had their own plans on their next drive. After Katin Houser led the orange and blue all the way down the field, tight end Davin Stoffel played the hero with just 13 seconds remaining in the first half. Stoffel caught the ball and was immediately picked up by three different Iowa defenders; however, the senior was able to lunge at the goal line, just barely crossing it to get his first touchdown as an Illini. That play would be the last time the Illini would score on Saturday. Both teams went to the locker room tied 17 -17, and one team didn’t leave that mark. It felt like every time Iowa needed just a few more yards in the second half, they’d always be able to muscle out the needed distance. On the contrary, the Illini couldn’t stop coming up short in the second half. It’s not the end you want on senior night, but Illinois will have two more chances this season. Moments that Mattered I think Illinois has a serious talent in Trimble going forward. Things we love to see ⤵️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/3INdDEuwdx — Hawkeye Football (@HawkeyeFootball) November 21, 2026 Illinois had all the momentum goin

item.title: Ithaca football tops Menominee to reach Division 7 state final
item.description: The Ithaca football team is headed to Ford Field. Gibson Rondy and Greyson Merchant each scored multiple touchdowns to lead the Yellowjackets to a 34-26 victory over Menominee in a Division 7 state semifinal at Gaylord High School on Saturday, Nov. 21. The win helps Ithaca (12-1) advance to its first state championship game since 2017. The Yellowjackets will face Ottawa Lake Whiteford at Ford Field on Saturday, Nov. 28. Rondy had 21 carries for 180 yards and three touchdowns and threw for 60 yards, while Merchant added a touchdown run and returned a kickoff 94 yards for a score to lead the Yellowjackets. Ithaca trailed 20-14 at halftime but took the lead on a 57-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and then the Landon Bratschi extra point that followed. Merchant added a 10-yard TD run in the third. Menominee, the reigning Division 7 state champion, tightened the game on a 1-yard run by Jackson Myszak in the fourth quarter. But Rondy added a 5-yard touchdown run later in the quarter for Ithaca to answer the score. More: Four downs from DeWitt football's state semifinal loss to Zeeland West This article originally appeared on Lansing State Journal: Ithaca football tops Menominee to reach Division 7 state final

Despite boasting an explosive top-six offense anchored by Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen, the Cleveland Cavaliers have stumbled out of the gates to an underwhelming 9-8 start. After reaching the Eastern Conference Finals last spring, Cleveland currently sits seventh in the East and ranks just 21st in defensive rating a sluggish opening month that has quietly put head coach Kenny Atkinson on notice. While Harden erupted for 51 points against Indiana to snap a mini-skid, Cleveland’s perimeter defense and wing scoring remain dangerously thin behind offseason pickup Peyton Watson and sharpshooter Sam Merrill. If team president Koby Altman wants to stabilize Atkinson’s rotation and rescue Cleveland’s championship aspirations before the pressure mounts, he should strike early and target New Orleans Pelicans forward Trey Murphy III . Adding Murphy III solves both problems in a single stroke. At 6-foot-8 and 26 years old, Murphy III is blossoming into one of the league’s premier two-way wings, averaging 15.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game in New Orleans this season while draining high-volume three-pointers. Under Atkinson’s pace-and-space system, Murphy III would thrive as a lethal off-ball weapon who punishes defenses whenever teams blitz Mitchell or Harden in pick-and-rolls. Just as importantly, his length and athleticism give Cleveland a reliable point-of-attack defender who can check top Eastern Conference wings like Jayson Tatum and OG Anunoby without forcing Mobley to constantly abandon the paint. item.title: Devine football's Enoch Hall named Express-News Athlete of the Week
item.description: Enoch Hall is a junior running back/defensive back for Devine. (Courtesy/Devine football) Devine junior running back Enoch Hall has been a huge part of the Warhorses' resurgence this season. He proved it again last week in helping Devine accomplish something it hadn't done in over a decade - win a playoff game. For his part in that feat, Hall has been voted the Express-News Athlete of the Week. Hall rushed for 217 yards and five touchdowns on just 15 carries in a 69-21 win over Randolph in the first round of the Class 3A Division I playoffs. It was the Warhorses' first playoff win since 2015. He's been the offensive engine for the Warhorses all season. He earned Offensive Player of the Week earlier this season in a 47-6 win over Poteet in which he rushed for 160 yards on 14.5 yards per carry and scored five touchdowns. This week, he beat out four fellow finalists in the poll to earn Athlete of the Week honors. Steele junior Pike Kempe earned his third Defensive Player of the Week award of the season in helping the Knights win their playoff opener last week. He made 22 tackles, including eight solo stops and three TFLs, to lead Steele to a 44-24 win over Reagan in the Class 6A Division I bracket. Judson senior Kayden Graham rushed for a career-high 272 yards and four touchdowns on 38 carries to lead the Rockets to a 63-53 win over Brandeis in the first round of the Class 6A Division II playoffs. He was named Offensive Player of the Week for his efforts. Wagner senior Kyzarriah Fox was named Girls Basketball Player of the Week after she earned tournament MVP honors at the Judson ISD Tip Off in the 'Tone. She averaged 16 points, 10 rebounds, 3.4 steals and 1.8 assists in helping the Rockets take the tournament title. She also scored 19 points with 17 rebounds in a midweek win over Sotomayor. Southwest sophomore Skylar Sims averaged 17.8 points, 13.1 rebounds, 3 assists and 2.6 steals at the Harlandale ISD tournament. She had 24 points, 17 rebounds, four assists and five steals in win over Clemens and 19 points and 16 rebounds in an OT loss against McCollum in the championship. item.title: Leistikow's 4 thoughts on Iowa's aggressive 34-17 win at Illinois
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Illinois — Some help in the college football world started to roll in for the playoff-contending Iowa Hawkeyes . As the Nov. 21 game against Illinois wore on before a sellout crowd of 60,670 at Memorial Stadium, the question became: Could they take advantage? The No. 15 Hawkeyes stayed bold, stayed aggressive and unlocked an impressive 34-17 win against Illinois to move to 9-2 overall, 6-2 in the Big Ten Conference. Now Nebraska, which upset No. 14 Ohio State earlier in the day, stands in the way of a 10-2 season and a possible College Football Playoff berth Nov. 27 at Kinnick Stadium. The defining moment of the game came on a fourth-and-goal call from Illinois’ 2½-yard line with 7 minutes, 28 seconds remaining. Iowa had started the drive at its own 9-yard line and marched the length of the field in a clock-churning possession that spanned the third and fourth quarters. Iowa expended all three timeouts on the drive, including on the play to set up this pivotal call. In a decision that rekindled the daring fourth-and-goal call in the final minutes vs. Oregon last season with Mark Gronowski, offensive coordinator Tim Lester dialed up a quarterback draw in an empty backfield. And Hank Brown, the pro-style passer, made an electric juke and high-stepped into the end zone to give Iowa a 27-17 lead with a 2-yard touchdown. Things we love to see ⤵️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/3INdDEuwdx — Hawkeye Football (@HawkeyeFootball) November 21, 2026 BTN cameras showed Lester and analyst Scott Chandler exchanging an emphatic high-five to celebrate what became a game-clinching call. This might go down as the call of the year. If Brown can't juke linebacker James Kreutz at the 3-yard line and gets tackled, Iowa might not get the win. If Kirk Ferentz elected to kick the field goal, it would have invited an aggressive Illinois passing game to perhaps come back and win by one. Instead, Iowa kept the foot down, went for the throat, and buried the Illini in that moment. Brown's touchdown capped a soul-crushing drive that consumed 19 plays, 91 yards and 10:05 of game clock. The Hawkeye defense, which stayed fresh as the offense did its work, finished things off with Jaylen Watson's 40-yard interception-return touchdown up the left sideline with 2:56 remaining. Iowa’s secondary answers rough first half, extends pick-6 streak Remember when the Hawkeyes struggled in pass coverage? Iowa yielded 276 passing yards to Michigan’s Bryce Underwood on Sept. 26, then 324 the following week to Ohio State’s Julian Sayin, then 320 the following week in a blowout win at Washington. But they locked down Minnesota, Wisconsin, Northwestern and Purdue over the last month … then faced Illinois’ Katin Houser, a somewhat surprising starter for Illinois considering he started the week as “doubtful” on the injury report with what Illinois coach Bret Bielema said was a broken nose and concussion protocol. item.title: Mets Showing Interest In All-Star First Baseman After Resurgent Season
item.description: First baseman Ty France The New York Mets let Pete Alonso walk last offseason and were unable to replace his offensive production. The Mets have some internal options, but none of them really inspire confidence in the team's ability to replace Alonso. In reality, there is no replacement for a first baseman of Alonso's caliber. However, there is one option in free agency that could be a huge upgrade for the Mets: Ty France. According to the New York Post's Jon Heyman , the Mets are showing interest in France. France was an All-Star in 2022, and he was solid in 2023. However, he had been unable to replicate his 2022 success until last season. From 2023-2025, France had a .686 OPS. He hit 20 home runs in 2022, but had just 32 home runs in the three seasons right after that. Last year, France hit 21 home runs for the San Diego Padres and slashed .295/.363/.502. He has won a Gold Glove Award in his career and is still an elite defender at first base. David Stearns has often emphasized his desire to improve the Mets' defense, and adding France would certainly help. The Padres are reportedly interested in bringing France back, and he is reportedly looking for a three-year deal. The Mets and France seem like a perfect fit, but with the Mets expected to spend big on Tarik Skubal, they may not be able to compete with some of the other offers France gets. item.title: 'Perfect so far today': Louis Riddick, Bob Wischusen put brutal announcer jinx on BYU kicker
item.description: Credit: ESPN Dread it, run from it, the announcer jinx arrives all the same. The BYU Cougars’ College Football Playoff hopes were on the line Saturday when kicker Matthias Dunn stepped onto the field with three seconds remaining to attempt a game-winning 37-yard field goal against the Kansas Jayhawks. If he made it, the Cougars would move to 9-2 and keep their national championship hopes alive. If he missed it, we head to overtime, where anything can happen. After the ESPN broadcast noted the length of the field goal attempt, game analyst Louis Riddick started saying, “What should be a routine,” but stopped himself, perhaps realizing what he was doing. The silence left behind was filled by play-by-play announcer Bob Wischusen, who completed the jinx. “Perfect from this distance during his career,” said Wischusen. “Perfect so far today, 3-for-3.” Obviously, you know what happened next. Louis Riddick: “What should be a routine…” Bob Wischusen: “Perfect from this distance during his career. Perfect so far today, 3-for-3.” https://t.co/aQtm6XWWNM — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 21, 2026 Thankfully for Dunn, the Cougars eventually won in triple overtime, but he had to sweat bullets the whole time until then. The dreaded announcer jinx has struck several times this college football season. And although some announcers explain it away as happenstance or claim they’re simply doing their job , we all know the truth. The post Louis Riddick, Bob Wischusen put brutal announcer jinx on BYU kicker appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Kai Trump’s Teammate Apologizes After Lying To LPGA Official
item.description: Michael Madrid-Imagn Images Scarlett Schremmer’s debut at The Annika ended in disqualification. The University of Miami sophomore admitted she lied to a rules official about using an illegal yardage book. Schremmer faced the tour after the disqualification dropped. She owns the mistake now, saying she was scared and made a poor choice. The rule is strict, and the LPGA does not bend for sponsor invites or college exceptions. The incident started when Schremmer played alongside Perrine Delacour and Dongeun Lee. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, carried her bag that day. Schremmer opened with a 69, but trouble brewed in the scoring tent. The LPGA received a tip after the first round about the book in her bag. When asked directly if she was using the unapproved yardage book, Schremmer said no. The tour later looked at photo evidence to confirm the breach. A video review showed the book was indeed present and in use. The Apology and the Lie Schremmer released a statement on Saturday to address the fallout. She spent days reflecting on how she handled the pressure of the moment. “Over the past few days, I’ve spent a lot of time reflecting on what happened last week and, more importantly, how I handled the situation,” she said, according to a report . She claimed she did not know the book had illegal info. When the official asked, fear took over. She admitted to saying the book was not in use. “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake,”. Schremmer noted that her actions did not reflect the values she tries to live by. She loves the game and knows what it means to be a competitor. Frustration on the Course Other players in the field felt the sting of this decision. Perrine Delacour took to Instagram to voice her anger on Saturday morning. She responded to a post about the situation, questioning the rules enforcement. “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies,” Delacour wrote. Her comment highlights a deeper issue with how the tour handles sponsor exemptions. Kai Trump was not involved in the rule break, but her presence drew eyes all week. She carried Schremmer’s bag at the practice facility. Trump even followed the round from outside the ropes with a Secret Service detail. Schremmer shot a 74 on Friday and missed the cut before the disqualification even hit. The tour review process moved fast once the video evidence surfaced. Integrity in the Modern Game The LPGA has a clear rule for yardage books under Model Local Rule G-11. Players may only use the book approved for that specific event. College rules differ, which might have confused Schremmer, but the lie remains the core problem. Breaking the rule is one thing; lying about it is another. Schremmer said she wanted to be the person who respects the standards of the game. She blamed herself for not checking the book before the round started. item.title: Kicker Smyth elevated to Saints' playing roster
item.description: [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth has been elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise. The former gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in Northern Ireland, has started the last two NFL games for the Saints after being promoted from the practice squad. The 25-year-old was handed a second opportunity to be the Saints' kicker after Dan Carlson, who started the season as first choice, was released at the start of November due to mixed form. Smyth helped the Saints to an overtime win over the Cleveland Browns on his return to the team and then kicked a late 55-yard field goal in the 20-17 defeat by the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. NFL rules state a player from a practice squad cannot be used more than three times in a season, and Smyth has been rewarded for his impressive return. He made his NFL debut for New Orleans last November but was released by the franchise in August. Smyth was retained on their practice squad due to having an exemption as he came through the NFL's international player pathway. His first game since signing his new deal is at the Chicago Bears on Sunday at 18:00 GMT. NFL fixtures and results Get American Football news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Bavarian Loan Works: 2. Bundesliga clubs interested in Bayern Munich youngster
item.description: Photo by Getty Images Bayern Munich’s young forward, Tom Binder, is getting a lot of attention from around Germany. According to reports from Transfermarkt (as recorded by @iMiaSanM ia ), several 2. Bundesliga teams have inquired about bringing Binder in on loan in the January window. According to Bild (also record ed by @iMiaSanM ia ), Dynamo Dresden seems to be the keenest on signing the forward. Dresden was close to signing Binder on loan this summer, but Bayern decided last minute to keep him in Munich. The decision not to let him leave on loan was heavily advocated for by manager Vincent Kompany and sporting director Christoph Freund, and was solidified by Arijon Ibrahimović’s loan to Augsburg. He was reportedly enticed to remain by the prospect of playing time. However, coming into this week, he only had one appearance for the senior team—15 minutes off the bench in the DFB-Pokal against Magdeburg—and just four appearances with two goals for the second team until this week. His number was called upon on Friday, when he made his Bundesliga debut against 1. FC Köln as a halftime sub for the injured Michael Olise. The decision to allow Binder to go out on loan will come down to Bayern’s personnel situation and how injuries look going into the transfer window in January. There are currently no indications that Bayern wil l let him leave in Janua ry, but if the opportunity presents itself, Dresden will be first in line to bring him in on loan. Join the conversation! item.title: Aljamain Sterling reacts to controversial loss to Kevin Vallejos at UFC Qatar: ‘What can you do?’
item.description: Aljamain Sterling suffered a tough loss at UFC Qatar | Ed Mulholland, Zuffa LLC Aljamain Sterling is not happy with the judges. On Saturday, Sterling fought Kevin Vallejos in the co-main event of UFC Qatar, and the former bantamweight champion had a rough night. The fight was extremely competitive, and despite having almost no success with his wrestling and grappling, Sterling clearly thought he did enough to edge out the victory; he was mistaken. All three judges scored the bout for Vallejos, with two even scoring the bout 30-27. When the decision was read, Sterling looked confused, and shortly afterward, he shared his thoughts on the decision on social media. What can you do? When you’re in there with someone and you’re landing more volume and making them miss. You would assume you’d edge out the fight. Maybe his cornermen cheering for wild strikeouts swayed the judges? Idk🤷🏾‍♂️ Tough luck tonight. Congrats Kevin. I’ve been down worse… — Aljamain Sterling (@funkmasterMMA) November 21, 2026 What can you do? When you’re in there with someone and you’re landing more volume and making them miss. You would assume you’d edge out the fight. Maybe his cornermen cheering for wild strikeouts swayed the judges? Idk Tough luck tonight. Congrats Kevin. I’ve been down worse and came back. Appreciate the support Per UFC Stats , Vallejos actually out-landed Sterling in significant strikes over three rounds, 37 to 32, and landed at a high percentage as well, 39% to 34%. However, Sterling did slightly edge Vallejos in significant strikes in the first round and second round, landing one more in each. He also successfully landed one takedown in 12 attempts. The loss stops a two-fight winning streak for Sterling and, at least for now, bumps him out of the featherweight title picture. Vallejos, meanwhile, moves to 5-0 in the UFC and called for a title shot after the win.

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached a climax with the fixtures for the first finals weekend confirmed. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. Northern Hemisphere table Team Played Won Lost Points Difference Points 1. France 6 5 1 +108 26 2. item.title: Terrorists kill Niger village head, five others, abduct residents
item.description: …Governor Bago deploys joint security team to affected community By Clare Nnabuike, Minna Suspected terrorists have killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, and five other residents in an attack that also left several people abducted and houses burnt. The attackers reportedly invaded the community at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, shortly after the Muslim call to prayer, forcing residents to flee into nearby bushes for safety. Sources in the community alleged that the assailants beheaded the village head and burnt his body. They also reported that a newborn baby died after being left inside a house that was set ablaze during the attack. Several residents were reportedly abducted, although the exact number of those taken away had yet to be established. Some residents also alleged that individuals from the community had collaborated with the attackers. However, the claims had not been independently verified as of the time of filing this report. The Niger State Police Command confirmed the attack, saying five people were killed and that joint security teams had been deployed to the area to apprehend the perpetrators. The Police Public Relations Officer, Wasiu Abiodun, said in a statement that the incident was reported at about 5:00 a.m. on November 21. “On 21/11/2026 at about 5am, report received indicated that suspected armed men invaded Lumma Ba’are village, Borgu LGA and attacked the community, while about five persons reportedly lost their lives during the attack. “Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” Abiodun stated. Also confirming the incident, the Niger State Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Obed Nuhu Nana, said five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they were receiving medical attention. In a statement, Nana said the attack occurred amid lingering intercommunal tensions in the area, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable. “The Niger State Government condemns the attack on Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area, which claimed the lives of five persons, including the Village Head, Malam Bawa Muhammad. “The attack, according to reports received, occurred at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, when suspected armed men invaded the community amid lingering intercommunal tensions and launched an assault on residents. “Five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they are currently receiving medical attention. Some houses were also reportedly set ablaze during the incident,” the statement said. item.title: Customs seize contraband worth N3.52bn in Ogun
item.description: .recover cannabis, codeine syrup, others By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted and seized contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion as part of intensified efforts to curb smuggling, protect public health and safeguard the nation’s economy. The seizures, which include 6,037 wraps of cannabis, 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup, more than 1.45 million tablets and capsules of various brands, foreign parboiled rice, petroleum products and vehicles, were inspected and paraded by the Comptroller-General of Customs during a visit to the Command. According to a statement issued on Saturday, by the Public Relations Officer of Ogun I Area Command, Assistant Superintendent of Customs Paul Gimba, the total value of the seized items with available valuations stood at **₦3,517,838,700. The statement said the seizures reflected the Command’s sustained efforts to combat smuggling and prevent the circulation of prohibited and potentially harmful products in the country. A breakdown of the intercepted items showed that cannabis accounted for 6,037 wraps, valued at ₦1.268 billion, while 20,500 bottles of cough syrup containing codeine had a Duty Paid Value of ₦147.6 million. The Command also intercepted 828,920 tablets of different brands valued at ₦795.76 million and 627,320 capsules worth ₦376.39 million. Other pharmaceutical products seized included 2,850 ampoules of Enox 4000 injection, valued at ₦17.1 million, and 95 prostate pills worth ₦570,000. The seizures further included 5,173 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, valued at ₦455.22 million, alongside 1,067 used tyres worth ₦52.82 million. In the petroleum products category, Customs intercepted 1,037 kegs of 25 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦34.22 million, and 1,008 kegs of 25 litres of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), worth ₦44.35 million. Other seized items comprised 21 packages of walkie-talkies, 185 packages of sanitary pads and diapers valued at ₦18.13 million, 125 live cartridges and two trucks with a combined valuation of ₦144 million. The Command also recorded seizures of several used vehicles, including a 2024 Toyota RAV4 and Toyota Highlander valued at a combined ₦50 million; two Lexus vehicles worth ₦25 million; a 2000 Toyota Hilux valued at ₦11 million; a 2013 Toyota RAV4 worth ₦17 million; and a Toyota Sienna valued at ₦14.7 million. Other vehicles intercepted were a 2010 Toyota Venza valued at ₦14.6 million, an Opel worth ₦7.3 million, a Mazda valued at ₦7.1 million and a 2012 Range Rover Sport worth ₦17.2 million. The Customs Service said the interceptions underscored the Command’s determination to enforce relevant Customs laws, prevent the importation and circulation of prohibited goods and protect Nigeria’s economic interests. Rising profile of Tems, Asake and Nigerian artists’ Grammy journey
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi The voices are getting louder everyday that Asake and Tems are the new King and Queen of Afrobeats respectively. And the Recording Academy confirmed it on November 16, 2026 when it announced the nominees for 2027 Grammy awards. Asake appears just to be coming to his own with two nominations while Tems shatfers the roof with four Grammy nominations in one year. Tems has emerged as Nigeria’s most successful representative in the latest nomination cycle, earning four nominations and further establishing herself as one of the most versatile Nigerian musicians on the international stage. Her recognition in the R&B categories is particularly noteworthy. It demonstrates that her appeal extends beyond the African music market and that her songwriting and vocal abilities are attracting recognition in mainstream American music. The nominations also build on an impressive Grammy history. Tems won her first Grammy in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake, which won Best Melodic Rap Performance. She subsequently won Best African Music Performance in 2025 for her reimagining of “Love Me JeJe”. She has also received recognition for her contribution to Beyoncé’s Renaissance, Wizkid’s “Essence” and Rihanna’s “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack. With two Grammy victories already to her credit, Tems is approaching the 2027 ceremony with an opportunity to increase her collection and further strengthen Nigeria’s presence in international R&B. Asake on the other hand has not won any Grammy – yet. But he appears to be knocking on the door. The “Lonely at the Top” hitmaker has now received four Grammy Award nominations as of November 2026. His nominations are all in the Best African Music Performance category. His flirting with the Recording Academy started in 2024 with his hit “Amapiano” with Olamide, followed by “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. Once again, he has dragged Wizkid onto the Grammy ballot with their collaboration “Jogodo” and his own solo hit “Gratitude” in 2027 Six Nigerian stars earn 2027 Grammy nominations as Afrobeats expands global reach, with the country securing representation in Best African Music Performance, Best Global Music Album, Best Global Music Performance and Best R&B Song. Joining Tems and Asake on the list are: Burna Boy with one nomination for Dia Dia with Shakira for Best Global Music Performance; Wizkid has one nomination too, for his collaboration with Asake on “Jogodo”; Ayra Starr has two nominations for Best Global Music Album with her hit “Starrgirl” and Best African Music Performance on the “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” collaboration with Angélique Kidjo and Davido with one nomination as his album “Oriadé” earned a place in the Best Global Music Album category, where it will compete against projects by Tems, Ayra Starr, Anitta and Angélique Kidjo. item.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
item.description: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. (Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) The Fight Off the Pitch The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed. If the verdict stands, they face a heavy sanction, and a big points deduction is one of the options on the table. So Maresca could get everythi

item.title: Why some young women are rejecting marriage – Bimbo Akintola
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Bimbo Akintola has offered an insight into why some young women are becoming reluctant to embrace marriage, suggesting that their decisions may be influenced by the experiences of their mothers. Akintola made this observation in an interview with Nollywire while discussing her role in Dear Ajayi. According to the actress, some women are rejecting the idea of marriage because they do not want to find themselves in situations where they give everything to their families but have little left for themselves. “You see a lot of others rebelling and not wanting to be in that position of giving everything but having nothing. You see girls now who say, ‘I don’t want to get married. That’s not the life I want,’” she said. She added that some of these decisions stem from what younger women have witnessed in their mothers’ lives. “It’s because they look at their mother’s life and they say, ‘No, that is not the life I want,’” Akintola stated. The actress also advocated shared responsibility within families, arguing that caring for everyone should not become the burden of one individual. “We believe everybody should take care of everybody, or one person in the family will now be the one taking care of every other person, forgetting themselves,” she said. Offering a word of caution to women, Akintola emphasised the importance of self-care, noting that people can only give meaningfully to others when their own needs are met. “You can only give from a well that’s full. That’s the truth. If you yourself are not nourished, you are not taking care of yourself, whatever it is you are giving others is less than 50 per cent,” she said. She warned that constantly neglecting oneself while caring for others could eventually lead to resentment, hatred and irritability. The post Why some young women are rejecting marriage – Bimbo Akintola appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bayelsa tragedy boat had no manifest, passengers didn’t wear life jacket – Diri
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A visibly sad Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Douye Diri, has revealed that the boat involved in the Friday fatal accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area had no manifest, and the passengers did wear life jackets. Consequently, Governor Diri vowed that all negligent persons involved will face trial. The governor gave the directive on Saturday after visiting the scene of the accident at the Oweikorogha axis of the river. Also, he visited survivors at the Government House Specialist Hospital in Yenagoa. He directed the Commissioner of Police, the State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), and the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to commence investigation into the cause of the tragedy and submit a report in no distant time. Accompanied by Deputy Governor Dr. Peter Akpe, Deputy Speaker of the House of Assembly Michael Ogbere, and other top government officials, Diri in a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Daniel Alabrah, condoled with bereaved families and affected communities. “On behalf of the state government, I extend our condolences to the families that have lost their loved ones and the communities that were affected. “I hear there were more victims from Ukubie community where the boat was headed, but several other communities were also affected. So our heartfelt and sincere condolences go to the communities, to the families, and the rest of the state,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate and avoidable if every tier of government had done its job. “I believe that this should not have occurred if every department of government at the federal, state and local government diligently did their job. That is why I am going to institute a probe to ascertain what happened,” he said. Directing the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, the Commissioner of Police and the DSS State Director to investigate, he said: “The Honourable Commissioner, within your ministry, there must be an investigation into this incident. “The Commissioner of Police and the State Director of DSS, I want a report; an investigative report on what happened. All those who have played one role or the other, the law must surely catch up with all of them.” Diri expressed shock that the boat had no manifest and did not board passengers from the designated point at the jetty in Ayama community. No safety measures He also lamented that none of the passengers wore safety vests, despite the availability of life jackets provided by the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy and the state government. “I cannot imagine a boat like that had no manifest and did not board passengers at the designated point. Today, we have this tragedy on our hands. “So, CP and DSS, you have work to do. I want that report in no distant date from now, so that people will know that there is a government in place here,” he said. item.title: Pain of losing loved ones never goes away – RMD
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, has opened up about the emotional challenges of losing loved ones, describing grief as one of the hardest experiences he has had to deal with. The 65-year-old actor made this known during an appearance on At His Right Hand, a podcast hosted by Olive Emodi. Looking back at his personal experiences, RMD disclosed that losing his wife and mother remains a deeply painful part of his life. “Loss of dear people in my life is the hardest thing I have had to deal with. I have lost a wife, I have lost a mother. Loss is very difficult to deal with. The pain never goes away. “What happens is that the pain transitions, morphs into different things,” he said. Beyond grief, the actor also reflected on legacy and the responsibility of giving back, describing his current phase of life as one dedicated to pouring into others. “I am 65, and I am saying it’s your turn. One can always play an advisory role in nation building because you never stop building. I am in the legacy stage of my life. Just as people poured into my life, I think I need to pour into a lot of people’s lives,” he said. Speaking further about talent, the fashionable role interpreter maintained that natural abilities cannot remain suppressed indefinitely, insisting that talent will eventually find an outlet. “It’s a question of time. The stammerer will pronounce his or her father’s name. Same thing with talent. You can’t keep it down even if you try. Somehow, it will find its voice,” he said. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi is only hope Nigeria has this time – Cleopas
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of 2027 general elections, the national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has said its Presidential Candidate, Peter Obi is the only hope Nigeria has at this time. According to the party, Obi remains the only one of the presidential candidates seeking for the January 16 2027 Presidential election that has what it takes to protect the lives of Nigerians, re-position the economy and rebuild the country after the 2027 general elections. Speaking during the celebration of his 57th birthday in Yenegoa at the weekend, the National Chairman of the NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas urged Nigerians to exercise their patriotic responsibility by voting out President Bola Tinubu who he said has failed in protecting the citizens and implementing policies that would ensure a better standard of living for them. According to the NDC National Chairman, the country could not afford another four years under an administration that had failed to address the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and rising cost of living. He said the forthcoming election should serve as a referendum on the Tinubu administration, adding that a second-term mandate must be earned through demonstrable performance rather than political sentiment. “Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said. In a statement signed on Saturday by NDC national publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC National Chairman also urged Nigerians to assess the individual presidential candidates based on their track record, competence and their ability to properly analyse and address the country’s challenges rather than vote on the basis of religion and party loyalty. Stakeholders and members of the Party who attended the occasion, including members of Bayelsa State House of Assembly, candidates of the Party, religious leaders and associates described the Chairman of the Party as a humble, loving and visionary leader who’s commitment to service, good governance and human development has continued to inspire those around him. In the statement, Osa Director described Senator Cleopas as a man of ‘wisdom, maturity, and uncommon political dexterity’ who has transformed the NDC into a national brand that is the envy of many-indeed the biggest, strangest and fastest growing opposition party in Africa. item.title: Adebutu’s return to ballot could boost Tinubu’s votes in Ogun – APC chieftain
item.description: …says Ogun APC must unite to deliver 1.5m votes for Tinubu By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta A member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) and Vice Director-General, West, Ogun State Campaign Council, Hon. Abdulkabir Akinlade, has said the return of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, to the ballot could boost President Bola Tinubu’s votes in Ogun State in the 2027 general election. Akinlade, who spoke during an interaction with journalists in Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital, described Adebutu’s return to the ballot as a welcome development, arguing that a competitive election could stimulate greater voter participation and, ultimately, improve Tinubu’s electoral fortunes. He said Adebutu had indicated his willingness, alongside his supporters, to vote for Tinubu, expressing optimism that the development could contribute to the APC’s projected votes in the state. Akinlade said the APC could no longer afford to secure between 200,000 and 300,000 votes in Ogun State, urging party leaders and stakeholders to work towards delivering between 1.5 million and two million votes for Tinubu. He recalled that Tinubu secured approximately 314,000 votes in Ogun State in the 2023 presidential election, despite the state having more than two million registered voters then. The former lawmaker called on longstanding members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to accommodate returning members and new entrants, stressing that unity within the party was crucial to achieving its target of between 1.5 million and two million votes for Tinubu in 2027. Akinlade urged both groups to put their differences aside, acknowledging that members who stayed behind had made sacrifices to sustain the party’s structure when others left. The former lawmaker, who disclosed that some of his supporters had remained with him through different political movements since 2018, expressed appreciation for their loyalty, but appealed to them to embrace patience, understanding and reconciliation. He also appealed to aggrieved stakeholders of the party to close ranks and support the party’s candidates in the presidential and National Assembly elections before shifting their attention to the governorship and State House of Assembly contests. On the disagreements trailing the party’s primaries, Akinlade said the governor and other party leaders had made efforts to secure consensus candidates in several constituencies to minimise the rancour and divisions often associated with contested primaries. He added that a reconciliation committee headed by Senator Gbenga Obadara had been engaging aggrieved party members, with a view to resolving the disagreements and restoring confidence in the party. item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time. The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1). He will play Zverev in Sunday’s decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up. Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender’s showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin. He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris. However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours. “I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way that I wanted to, to be honest,” said the seven-time Grand Slam winner. “But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set… and ended up playing good tennis.” Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton. The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set. In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all. The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break. Shelton faltered with two unforced errors allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover. “I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well,” said Alcaraz. “Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-breaker… I’m excited for tomorrow.” Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time — a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September. Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence. In claiming that title in Paris, as well as the US Open crown, Zverev catapulted himself above Alcaraz and Sinner in the rankings to world No. 1. In a repeat of the 2021 Finals title match, which the 29-year-old German also won, Zverev saw off Russian Medvedev in straight sets. A tightly-contested first frame rattled to a tie-break, which the two-time major winner raced through as Medvedev crumbled, failing to win a point.
